docs.title: Watch the demo
docs.text:
SuperQuantX 0.3.0 · Local simulation · No quantum hardware used · Watch on YouTube

SuperQuantX is an experimental, open-source toolkit for quantum machine learning and optimisation research. One API runs the same circuits and algorithms on PennyLane, Qiskit, Cirq, Amazon Braket, pytket and a built-in simulator, and every result comes with a classical reference so you can see whether the quantum part earns its keep.

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• One API, six gate-model backends: identical circuits, bit order normalised across SDKs.
  • Algorithms with built-in checks: VQE reports the exact ground energy, QAOA reports the brute-force optimum, classifiers can be benchmarked with compare_to_classical.
  • Benchmarking protocol: equal tuning budgets, identical folds and a corrected t-test, following arXiv:2610.42029.
  • Agents that show their work: portfolio and classification agents return the classical optimum or baseline alongside the quantum answer.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Get started with SuperQuantX in minutes:

import superquantx as sqx

# Choose your backend
backend = sqx.get_backend('simulator')

# Create a quantum circuit
circuit = backend.create_circuit(n_qubits=2)
circuit = backend.add_gate(circuit, 'H', 0)  # Hadamard gate
circuit = backend.add_gate(circuit, 'CNOT', [0, 1])  # CNOT gate
circuit = backend.add_measurement(circuit)

# Execute the circuit
result = backend.execute_circuit(circuit, shots=1024)
print(f"Results: {result['counts']}")

docs.title: Backend Overview
docs.text:
SuperQuantX 0.3.0 exposes one portable gate-model API across several frameworks, plus a separate Ocean backend for annealing. Prefer the per-backend guides for detail:

Backend Guide Local default Notes Simulator simulator always Pure Python, fluent circuit.h API PennyLane pennylane default.qubit Best for variational / QML work Qiskit qiskit Aer simulator IBM Quantum needs credentials Cirq cirq local Cirq simulator Google hardware needs credentials Braket braket local Braket SV AWS / IonQ / Rigetti need credentials TKET tket Aer via pytket-qiskit Quantinuum hardware needs credentials Ocean ocean simulated annealing QUBO / Ising, not gate circuits

docs.title: Portable Gate-Model Pattern
docs.text:
import numpy as np
import superquantx as sqx

for name in ["simulator", "pennylane", "qiskit", "cirq", "braket", "tket"]:
    backend = sqx.get_backend(name)
    circuit = backend.create_circuit(2)
    circuit = backend.add_gate(circuit, "H", 0)
    circuit = backend.add_gate(circuit, "CNOT", [0, 1])
    circuit = backend.add_measurement(circuit)
    counts = backend.execute_circuit(circuit, shots=200)["counts"]
    print(name, counts)

docs.title: Hardware Access
docs.text:
Hardware constructors accept credentials but are not exercised in CI.

Requires credentials

IBM Quantum, AWS Braket QPUs, Quantinuum and D-Wave Leap all need accounts. Snippets below are API-checked only.

import superquantx as sqx

# IBM Quantum (Qiskit Runtime)
ibm = sqx.QiskitBackend(device="ibm_brisbane", shots=1024)

# Amazon Braket QPU
braket = sqx.BraketBackend(
    device="arn:aws:braket:us-east-1::device/qpu/ionq/Forte-1",
    s3_folder=("my-braket-bucket", "runs"),
    shots=100,
)

# D-Wave Leap
ocean = sqx.OceanBackend(device="advantage", token="YOUR_DWAVE_LEAP_TOKEN")

There is no separate quantinuum backend name in 0.3.0; use tket locally. Quantinuum cloud access needs pytket-quantinuum, which is not part of the superquantx[tket] extra.

docs.title: SuperQuantX MCP Server for AI Assistants
docs.text:
SuperQuantX ships a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so that AI assistants such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, or any MCP client can build and run quantum circuits, compare backends, and run small quantum machine learning and optimization experiments through one unified API.

The server speaks MCP over stdio, uses the official mcp Python SDK (2.x), and runs on simulators only by default.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Run the server with no install step (uvx fetches the pinned release into an isolated environment):

uvx --from "superquantx[mcp]==0.3.0" superquantx-mcp

Or add it to a uv project, with optional Qiskit and PennyLane backends:

uv add "superquantx[mcp,qiskit,pennylane]==0.3.0"
uv run superquantx-mcp
# or, from a checkout
uv pip install ".[mcp,qiskit,pennylane]"
# or with pip
pip install "superquantx[mcp,qiskit,pennylane]==0.3.0"

The mcp extra needs Python 3.10 or newer (SuperQuantX itself requires 3.11+). The built-in simulator backend works with no extra SDK, so uv add "superquantx[mcp]==0.3.0" is enough to try it.

Two equivalent entry points start the server on stdio:

superquantx-mcp
python -m superquantx.mcp

Both are meant to be launched by an MCP client, not used interactively. superquantx-mcp --help prints the supported environment variables.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Tool What it does list_backends Every SuperQuantX backend with SDK install status, initialization, and a 2 qubit Bell smoke test. Status is working, not_installed, init_failed, execution_failed, or wrong_results. backend_versions Installed versions of SuperQuantX, Python, numpy/scipy/scikit-learn, every quantum SDK, and per-backend version info. run_circuit Run a circuit given as OpenQASM 2, OpenQASM 3, or a JSON gate list. Returns counts, probabilities, gate counts, and timing (parse, backend init, execute, total). bell_state_demo Run the same Bell circuit on several backends and report how many shots are correlated (00 or 11). qsvm_classify Quantum kernel SVM (SuperQuantX QuantumSVM) on a toy dataset or your own data, with kernel diagnostics and an RBF SVM baseline on the same split. qaoa_maxcut QAOA for MaxCut on a small graph with a classical optimizer, checked against exact brute force.

Every tool returns structured JSON with "ok": true or "ok": false plus an error object. Tools never raise: bad input comes back as ValidationError, and a backend failure is reported for that backend only (for example bell_state_demo still returns results for the backends that work).

docs.title: Circuit input formats
docs.text:
OpenQASM 2:

OPENQASM 2.0;
include "qelib1.inc";
qreg q[2];
creg c[2];
h q[0];
cx q[0],q[1];
measure q -> c;

OpenQASM 3 (qubit[n] / bit[n] declarations, c = measure q;) is accepted too. The parser supports a safe subset: standard gates (id x y z h s sdg t tdg sx rx ry rz p u1 u2 u3 u cx cz swap ccx and common aliases such as cnot, toffoli, phase), register broadcast (h q;), parameter expressions with pi and basic math (rz(-3*pi/4) q[0];). Gate definitions, classical control flow, and reset are rejected with a clear message. measure and barrier are accepted and ignored, since every qubit is measured at the end.

JSON gate list (a list, or an object with n_qubits and gates):

{"n_qubits": 2, "gates": [
  {"gate": "ry", "qubits": [0], "params": ["pi/3"]},
  {"gate": "cx", "qubits": [0, 1]}
]}

Parameters may be numbers or expression strings such as "pi/3", evaluated without eval.

Bit order. Counts are little-endian, the Qiskit convention: qubit 0 is the rightmost bit. All backends are normalized to this order (PennyLane results are reversed internally).

docs.title: Notes on qsvm_classify
docs.text:
• Datasets: moons, circles, blobs, xor (2 features) and iris (versicolor vs virginica, 4 features). Or pass X, y (and optionally X_test, y_test).
  • kernel="statevector" (default) computes the exact fidelity kernel |<phi(a)|phi(b)>|^2 from the statevectors of a Qiskit-convention ZZFeatureMap (or ZFeatureMap) produced by the selected backend SDK, then trains SuperQuantX QuantumSVM with it. Simulator, Qiskit, and PennyLane give identical kernels for the same data.
  • kernel="backend" uses the backend's own compute_kernel_matrix. Since 0.3.0 this is a fidelity kernel built from real quantum states. The tool reports kernel_diagnostics.looks_valid and warns if the diagonal deviates from one or a backend reports a fallback.
  • bandwidth (default 0.5) scales features before encoding. Smaller bandwidths usually generalize better on these toy sets (see Shaydulin and Wild, "Importance of kernel bandwidth in quantum machine learning", Phys. Rev. A 106, 042407, 2022).
  • A classical RBF SVM baseline is always reported unless classical_baseline=false. On these toy datasets the RBF baseline is often as good or better. Nothing here is evidence of quantum advantage.

docs.title: Notes on qaoa_maxcut
docs.text:
• edges is [[u, v], ...] or [[u, v, weight], ...], nodes 0..n-1.
  • Circuit: Hadamards, then per layer cx, rz(2*gamma*w), cx for every edge and rx(2*beta) mixers, executed through the SuperQuantX unified backend API. Parameters come from a coarse grid search refined with COBYLA (scipy).
  • The result includes the exact brute-force optimum, the approximation ratio (expected cut divided by max cut), the probability of sampling an optimal cut, and found_optimum.

docs.title: Limits and safety
docs.text:
Inputs are validated and capped. Defaults can be lowered or raised with environment variables, but never above the hard ceiling:

Variable Default Hard ceiling SUPERQUANTX_MCP_MAX_QUBITS 10 16 SUPERQUANTX_MCP_MAX_SHOTS 10000 100000 SUPERQUANTX_MCP_MAX_GATES 500 2000 SUPERQUANTX_MCP_MAX_QASM_CHARS 20000 50000 SUPERQUANTX_MCP_MAX_SAMPLES 80 200 SUPERQUANTX_MCP_MAX_FEATURES 4 6 SUPERQUANTX_MCP_MAX_QAOA_NODES 10 12 SUPERQUANTX_MCP_MAX_QAOA_LAYERS 3 4

Hardware is off by default. Tools only use local simulators (simulator, Qiskit Aer, PennyLane default.qubit, and the default local devices of the other SDKs). Passing a device to run_circuit is refused unless the server was started with SUPERQUANTX_MCP_ALLOW_HARDWARE=1, and even then the backend SDK's own credentials and configuration are required. Annealing-only backends (D-Wave Ocean) are listed but not used for gate circuits.

All tools are annotated read-only and do not touch the filesystem. Logs go to stderr so they never corrupt the stdio protocol stream.

docs.title: Client configuration
docs.text: Use the absolute path of the superquantx-mcp script from the environment where you installed SuperQuantX (which superquantx-mcp).

docs.title: Claude Desktop
docs.text:
Edit claude_desktop_config.json (macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/, Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "superquantx": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/venv/bin/superquantx-mcp",
      "args": [],
      "env": {
        "SUPERQUANTX_MCP_MAX_QUBITS": "10"
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Cursor
docs.text:
Create .cursor/mcp.json in your project (or ~/.cursor/mcp.json for all projects):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "superquantx": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "superquantx.mcp"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Without a pre-made virtualenv (uvx)
docs.text:
Since 0.3.0, uvx can run the server in an isolated environment:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "superquantx": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--from", "superquantx[mcp,qiskit,pennylane]==0.3.0", "superquantx-mcp"]
    }
  }
}

Use SuperQuantX 0.3.0 or newer; 0.2.0 does not include the MCP server.

docs.title: Programmatic client
docs.text:
examples/mcp_client_demo.py launches the server over stdio with the official SDK client and calls every tool:

Requires a running MCP client session

Illustrates the official MCP Python client; skipped in the docs checker because it launches a subprocess server.

import asyncio
from mcp import ClientSession, StdioServerParameters
from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client

params = StdioServerParameters(command="python", args=["-m", "superquantx.mcp"])

async def main():
    async with stdio_client(params) as (read, write):
        async with ClientSession(read, write) as client:
            await client.initialize()
            result = await client.call_tool("bell_state_demo", {"shots": 1000})
            print(result)

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: How it relates to the IBM Qiskit MCP servers
docs.text:
IBM maintains Qiskit MCP servers for the Qiskit stack (Qiskit, Qiskit IBM Runtime, the IBM transpiler service, and Qiskit Code Assistant). Those are the right choice for deep IBM Quantum workflows such as managing Runtime jobs on IBM hardware.

The SuperQuantX server is complementary: it is multi-backend. One circuit, one call, and the assistant can compare the built-in simulator, Qiskit Aer, PennyLane, and (when installed) Cirq, Braket, and TKET backends, plus ready-made QML and optimization experiments with classical baselines. You can enable both servers in the same client.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Everything runs on noiseless local simulators at toy scale (at most 16 qubits). Results show the workflow, not a quantum advantage.
  • Tested backends: built-in simulator, Qiskit Aer, PennyLane default.qubit. Cirq, Braket, and TKET go through the same unified backend code path but were not installed in the verification run.
  • The MCP QAOA tool has its own grid-search and COBYLA parameter search on top of the unified circuit API. The library's QAOA.solve also runs real circuits and reports a classical optimum. The MCP statevector QSVM mode retains its explicit Qiskit-convention encoding; backend mode uses the shared library feature maps, so the two modes can produce different valid kernels.

docs.title: Showcase
docs.text: examples/showcase.py is the five-minute demo of what SuperQuantX does today. It runs in about 10 seconds on a laptop, entirely on local simulators, and checks every quantum result against something classical.

docs.text:
A short silent walkthrough of SuperQuantX 0.3.0 on local simulators (backends, VQE/QAOA with classical checks, then MCP). Caption on the recording: SuperQuantX 0.3.0 · Local simulation · No quantum hardware used.

Watch on YouTube

uv sync --extra all-backends
uv run python examples/showcase.py
  1. Backends. Bell and GHZ circuits on every installed gate-model backend. Only the correct outcomes may appear.
  2. Quantum machine learning. A quantum kernel SVM on make_moons, compared with a tuned RBF SVM and logistic regression using the protocol of arXiv:2610.42029. See Benchmarking.
  3. Optimisation. QAOA on a 5-node MaxCut instance, checked against brute force.

2. Quantum kernel SVM vs tuned classical models (make_moons, pennylane)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
QuantumSVM (PennyLane), tuned       0.930 +/- 0.051      3.15s    25       119,000

3. QAOA MaxCut vs brute force (5 nodes, 7 edges, p=2, pennylane)
================================================================
QAOA best sampled cut : 01101  value 6
Brute-force optimum   : 01101  value 6
Expected cut of state : 5.019 (approximation ratio 0.837; a random cut averages 3.5)
Matches optimum       : yes   (484 circuit evaluations, 2.1s)

Total time 7.1s

docs.title: What this shows, and what it does not
docs.text:
• Six SDKs run the same circuits through one API and agree, after bit-order normalisation.
  • The tuned quantum kernel is competitive with classical models on this dataset, but not better: the difference from a tuned RBF SVM is not statistically significant. That matches the published evidence. Bandwidth tuning, not the circuit, is what lifts it from 0.67 to 0.93.
  • QAOA at depth 2 finds the optimal cut among its samples. Its expected cut (approximation ratio about 0.84) is what would matter on hardware, and brute force is instant at this size.
  • None of this is quantum advantage. All circuits are classically simulated.

docs.title: Agents demo
docs.text:
examples/quantum_agents_demo.py runs the portfolio agent (CVaR-VQE on a QUBO, checked against brute-force enumeration and a Markowitz reference) and the classification agent (which wraps compare_to_classical).

uv run python examples/quantum_agents_demo.py

docs.title: Quantum Agents API Reference
docs.text:
Quantum agents bundle one or more SuperQuantX algorithms behind a task-level interface. Every agent reports a classical baseline next to the quantum answer, computed in the same call, so you can see how the quantum result compares.

All examples on this page run on SuperQuantX 0.3.0 with the built-in simulator.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Agent What it does Classical check QuantumPortfolioAgent Picks k of n assets with CVaR-VQE on a mean-variance QUBO Brute-force optimum and a Markowitz solution QuantumOptimizationAgent Weighted MaxCut with QAOA, or a ground state with VQE Brute force or exact diagonalisation QuantumClassificationAgent Trains quantum classifiers, optionally as an ensemble Tuned RBF SVM and logistic regression on the same folds QuantumTradingAgent Experimental: portfolio selection only Same as the portfolio agent QuantumResearchAgent Experimental: VQE ground-state simulation only Exact diagonalisation

Agents do not report a "quantum advantage" figure. Features that are not implemented raise NotImplementedError instead of returning placeholder output.

docs.title: QuantumAgent
docs.text:
from superquantx.algorithms.quantum_agents import QuantumAgent


class MyQuantumAgent(QuantumAgent):
    def _initialize_agent(self):
        # Create the algorithms this agent uses and store them in self.algorithms
        pass

    def solve(self, problem_instance, **kwargs):
        # Return a QuantumResult, for example via self._result(result_dict, start_time)
        pass

    # QuantumAgent is a BaseQuantumAlgorithm, so fit and predict are required too
    def fit(self, X, y=None, **kwargs):
        self.is_fitted = True
        return self

    def predict(self, X, **kwargs):
        return X


agent = MyQuantumAgent(backend='simulator')
print(agent.get_agent_info()['agent_type'])

Constructor: QuantumAgent(backend, agent_config=None, shots=1024, **kwargs)

  • backend (str or backend): backend name such as 'simulator' or a backend instance
  • agent_config (dict, optional): configuration stored on the agent
  • shots (int): measurement shots
  • **kwargs: base algorithm options such as seed

Methods:

  • _initialize_agent(): abstract; create the agent's algorithms
  • solve(problem_instance, **kwargs): abstract; returns a QuantumResult
  • get_agent_info(): agent type, configuration, algorithms and metrics

Attributes: algorithms, results_history, performance_metrics, agent_config.

QuantumResult has the fields result (dict), metadata (dict), execution_time (seconds), backend_info, error and intermediate_results.

docs.title: QuantumPortfolioAgent
docs.text:
Selects n_select of n assets with equal weights. The selection problem is encoded as a diagonal Hamiltonian; a RealAmplitudes circuit is trained to minimise the CVaR of the energy, and the best sampled selection is returned. The brute-force optimum of the same QUBO and a long-only Markowitz portfolio are computed in the same call. Practical up to about 10 assets.

Constructor: QuantumPortfolioAgent(backend, n_select=None, risk_aversion=1.0, reps=2, alpha=0.25, n_restarts=5, maxiter=300, **kwargs)

  • n_select: number of assets to hold (default: half the assets)
  • risk_aversion: weight of the variance term
  • reps: ansatz repetitions
  • alpha: CVaR fraction (1.0 is ordinary VQE)
  • n_restarts, maxiter: optimizer restarts and iterations per restart
  • seed (keyword): makes the run reproducible

Methods:

  • fit(returns): estimate mean returns and covariance from a (periods x assets) matrix
  • solve(returns=None): run the selection; refits if returns are given
  • predict(returns=None): equal weights of the selected assets
import numpy as np
from superquantx import QuantumPortfolioAgent

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
returns = rng.multivariate_normal(
    mean=[0.08, 0.12, 0.10, 0.15],
    cov=[[0.16, 0.05, 0.03, 0.02],
         [0.05, 0.25, 0.04, 0.03],
         [0.03, 0.04, 0.20, 0.05],
         [0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0.30]],
    size=252,
) / 100

agent = QuantumPortfolioAgent(backend='simulator', n_select=2, risk_aversion=2.0, seed=0)
result = agent.solve(returns)
r = result.result

print("Quantum selection:     ", r['selected_assets'], r['weights'])
print("Brute-force selection: ", r['classical_selected_assets'])
print("Matches optimum:       ", r['matches_classical_optimum'])
print(f"P(optimum) after VQE:   {r['probability_of_optimum']:.3f}")
print(f"Expected return {r['expected_return']:.4f}, risk {r['risk']:.4f}")
print("Markowitz weights:     ", np.round(r['markowitz_reference']['weights'], 3))

Keys in result.result: selected_assets, weights, objective, feasible, classical_selected_assets, classical_objective, matches_classical_optimum, objective_gap, probability_of_optimum, optimum_sampled, markowitz_reference, expected_return, risk, sharpe_ratio, plus cvar_rescaled and shots.

Not available in 0.3.0

Black-Litterman or factor risk models, Sharpe or risk-parity objectives, per-asset weight limits and sector constraints are not implemented. The agent selects an equal-weight subset; use markowitz_reference for continuous weights.

docs.text:
import numpy as np
from superquantx import QuantumOptimizationAgent

# 4-node graph: edges (0,1), (1,2), (2,3), (3,0) with weight 1 and (0,2) with weight 2
adjacency = np.array([
    [0, 1, 2, 1],
    [1, 0, 1, 0],
    [2, 1, 0, 1],
    [1, 0, 1, 0],
], dtype=float)

agent = QuantumOptimizationAgent(backend='simulator', problem_type='combinatorial', p=2, seed=0)
result = agent.solve(adjacency)

print("Partition:", result.result['bitstring'])
print("Cut value:", result.result['cut_value'], "optimum:", result.result['classical_optimum'])
print("Approximation ratio:", round(result.result['approximation_ratio'], 3))
print("Algorithm:", result.metadata['algorithm_used'])

docs.title: Combining agents
docs.text:
Agents are ordinary Python objects, so you can chain them yourself:

import numpy as np
from superquantx import QuantumOptimizationAgent, QuantumPortfolioAgent

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
returns = rng.normal(0.001, 0.02, size=(250, 4))

portfolio = QuantumPortfolioAgent(backend='simulator', n_select=2, seed=0).solve(returns)
held = portfolio.result['selected_assets']

# Split the held assets' correlation graph with MaxCut
corr = np.abs(np.corrcoef(returns[:, held].T))
np.fill_diagonal(corr, 0)
split = QuantumOptimizationAgent(backend='simulator', seed=0).solve(corr)

print("Held:", held, "split:", split.result['bitstring'])
for name, res in [('portfolio', portfolio), ('maxcut', split)]:
    print(f"{name}: {res.execution_time:.2f}s, error={res.error}")

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from superquantx import QuantumResearchAgent, QuantumTradingAgent

try:
    QuantumTradingAgent(strategy='momentum').deploy(np.zeros((10, 3)))
except NotImplementedError as e:
    print("Not implemented:", e)

try:
    QuantumResearchAgent().investigate("Find a room-temperature superconductor")
except NotImplementedError as e:
    print("Not implemented:", e)

Invalid arguments raise ValueError, for example an unknown algorithm name in QuantumClassificationAgent or a problem_type other than 'combinatorial' or 'continuous'.

Choosing an agent

Start on the 'simulator' backend. Every agent accepts any SuperQuantX gate-model backend name, for example 'qiskit' or 'pennylane', once the matching extra is installed.

def __init__(
    self,
    backend: str | Any,
    shots: int = 1024,
    seed: int | None = None,
    optimization_level: int = 1,
    **kwargs
) -> None:
    """Initialize the quantum algorithm."""
    self.backend = self._initialize_backend(backend)
    self.shots = shots
    self.seed = seed
    self.optimization_level = optimization_level

    # Algorithm state
    self.is_fitted = False
    self.training_history = []
    self.best_params = None
    self.best_score = None

    # Store additional parameters
    self.algorithm_params = kwargs

    # Performance tracking
    self.execution_times = []
    self.backend_stats = {}

    logger.info(f"Initialized {self.__class__.__name__} with backend {type(self.backend).__name__}")

def save_model(self, filepath: str) -> None:
    """Save the trained model to disk.

    Args:
        filepath: Path where to save the model

    """
    import pickle

    if not self.is_fitted:
        logger.warning("Model is not fitted yet. Saving unfitted model.")

    model_data = {
        'class': self.__class__.__name__,
        'params': self.get_params(),
        'is_fitted': self.is_fitted,
        'training_history': self.training_history,
        'best_params': self.best_params,
        'best_score': self.best_score,
    }

    with open(filepath, 'wb') as f:
        pickle.dump(model_data, f)

    logger.info(f"Model saved to {filepath}")

@classmethod
def load_model(cls, filepath: str) -> 'BaseQuantumAlgorithm':
    """Load a trained model from disk.

    Args:
        filepath: Path to the saved model

    Returns:
        Loaded algorithm instance

    """
    import pickle

    with open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
        model_data = pickle.load(f)

    # Create new instance with saved parameters
    instance = cls(**model_data['params'])
    instance.is_fitted = model_data['is_fitted']
    instance.training_history = model_data['training_history']
    instance.best_params = model_data['best_params']
    instance.best_score = model_data['best_score']

    logger.info(f"Model loaded from {filepath}")
    return instance

def benchmark(self, X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray | None = None, runs: int = 5) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Benchmark algorithm performance.

    Args:
        X: Test data
        y: Test labels (optional)
        runs: Number of benchmark runs

    Returns:
        Benchmark results dictionary

    """
    execution_times = []
    scores = []

    for i in range(runs):
        start_time = time.time()

        if y is not None:
            score = self.score(X, y)
            scores.append(score)
        else:
            self.predict(X)

        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        execution_times.append(execution_time)

    results = {
        'execution_times': execution_times,
        'mean_execution_time': np.mean(execution_times),
        'std_execution_time': np.std(execution_times),
        'min_execution_time': np.min(execution_times),
        'max_execution_time': np.max(execution_times),
    }

    if scores:
        results.update({
            'scores': scores,
            'mean_score': np.mean(scores),
            'std_score': np.std(scores),
            'min_score': np.min(scores),
            'max_score': np.max(scores),
        })

    return results

QuantumSVM(backend: str | Any, feature_map: str | Any | None = 'ZZFeatureMap', feature_map_reps: int = 2, C: float = 1.0, gamma: float | None = None, quantum_kernel: Callable | None = None, shots: int = 1024, normalize_data: bool = True, auto_feature_map_mode: str = 'auto', **kwargs)

Bases: SupervisedQuantumAlgorithm

Quantum Support Vector Machine for classification.

This implementation uses quantum feature maps to transform data into a high-dimensional Hilbert space where linear separation is possible. The quantum kernel is computed using quantum circuits.

The algorithm works by: 1. Encoding classical data into quantum states using feature maps 2. Computing quantum kernels between data points 3. Training a classical SVM using the quantum kernel matrix

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default backend str | Any

Quantum backend for circuit execution

required feature_map str | Any | None

Feature map name ('ZZFeatureMap', 'PauliFeatureMap', 'AmplitudeMap', 'AngleEncoding', 'ZFeatureMap'), a custom object, or "auto" / None to select via the Qmes-inspired recommender.

Number of repetitions in the feature map

2 C float

Regularization parameter for SVM

1.0 gamma float | None

Quantum kernel bandwidth. Features are multiplied by gamma before encoding (after standardisation). Tuning it matters: small bandwidths avoid exponential kernel concentration (Shaydulin and Wild, 2022). None means 1.0.

None quantum_kernel Callable | None

def __init__(
    self,
    backend: str | Any,
    feature_map: str | Any | None = 'ZZFeatureMap',
    feature_map_reps: int = 2,
    C: float = 1.0,
    gamma: float | None = None,
    quantum_kernel: Callable | None = None,
    shots: int = 1024,
    normalize_data: bool = True,
    auto_feature_map_mode: str = 'auto',
    **kwargs
) -> None:
    super().__init__(backend=backend, shots=shots, **kwargs)

    self.feature_map = feature_map
    self.feature_map_reps = feature_map_reps
    self.C = C

def fit(self, X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, **kwargs) -> 'QuantumSVM':
    """Train the quantum SVM.

    Args:
        X: Training data features
        y: Training data labels
        **kwargs: Additional training parameters

    Returns:
        Self for method chaining

    """
    logger.info(f"Training QuantumSVM on {X.shape[0]} samples with {X.shape[1]} features")

    # Validate and preprocess data
    super().fit(X, y, **kwargs)

    if self.normalize_data:
        X = self.scaler.fit_transform(X)

    self.X_train_ = X.copy()

    # Resolve auto/manual feature map, then build the circuit
    resolved = self._resolve_feature_map_name(X, y)
    self.feature_map_circuit_ = self._create_feature_map(X.shape[1], resolved)

    # Compute quantum kernel matrix
    logger.info("Computing quantum kernel matrix...")
    self.kernel_matrix_ = self._compute_quantum_kernel(X)

    # Train classical SVM with quantum kernel
    self.svm = SVC(
        kernel='precomputed',
        C=self.C,
    )

    self.svm.fit(self.kernel_matrix_, y)
    self.is_fitted = True

    # Training accuracy straight from the training kernel (X is already scaled)
    train_predictions = self.svm.predict(self.kernel_matrix_)
    train_accuracy = accuracy_score(y, train_predictions)

    self.training_history.append({
        'train_accuracy': train_accuracy,
        'n_support_vectors': self.svm.n_support_,
        'kernel_matrix_shape': self.kernel_matrix_.shape,
        'selected_feature_map': self.selected_feature_map_,
        'feature_map_recommendation': self.feature_map_recommendation_,
    })

    logger.info(f"Training completed. Accuracy: {train_accuracy:.3f}, "
               f"Support vectors: {sum(self.svm.n_support_)}")

    return self

def analyze_kernel(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Analyze properties of the quantum kernel.

    Returns:
        Dictionary with kernel analysis results

    """
    if self.kernel_matrix_ is None:
        raise ValueError("Model must be fitted to analyze kernel")

    K = self.kernel_matrix_

    # Compute kernel properties
    eigenvalues = np.linalg.eigvals(K)

    analysis = {
        'kernel_shape': K.shape,
        'kernel_rank': np.linalg.matrix_rank(K),
        'condition_number': np.linalg.cond(K),
        'trace': np.trace(K),
        'frobenius_norm': np.linalg.norm(K, 'fro'),
        'eigenvalue_stats': {
            'mean': np.mean(eigenvalues),
            'std': np.std(eigenvalues),
            'min': np.min(eigenvalues),
            'max': np.max(eigenvalues),
        },
        'is_positive_definite': np.all(eigenvalues > 0),
    }

    return analysis

def fit(self, X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, **kwargs) -> 'QuantumNN':
    """Train the quantum neural network.

    Args:
        X: Training data features
        y: Training data labels
        **kwargs: Additional training parameters

    Returns:
        Self for method chaining

    """
    logger.info(f"Training QuantumNN on {X.shape[0]} samples with {X.shape[1]} features")

    # Validate and preprocess data
    super().fit(X, y, **kwargs)

    # Set number of classes for classification BEFORE building network
    if self.task_type == 'classification':
        unique_classes = np.unique(y)
        self.n_classes_ = len(unique_classes)
        logger.info(f"Detected {self.n_classes_} classes for classification: {unique_classes}")

    # Scale features
    X = self.scaler.fit_transform(X)

    # Encode labels for classification after setting n_classes_
    if self.task_type == 'classification' and self.encoder:
        y = self.encoder.fit_transform(y)

    # Determine network architecture
    self.n_qubits = self._determine_qubits(X.shape[1])
    self._build_network()

    # Reset training history
    self.loss_history = []
    self.accuracy_history = []

    logger.info(f"Training network with {self.n_qubits} qubits and {self.n_params} parameters")

    # Training loop
    for epoch in range(self.max_epochs):
        epoch_losses = []
        epoch_accuracies = []

        # Mini-batch training
        for i in range(0, len(X), self.batch_size):
            X_batch = X[i:i + self.batch_size]
            y_batch = y[i:i + self.batch_size]

            # Forward pass
            y_pred = self._forward_pass(X_batch, self.weights)

            # Compute loss
            loss = self._compute_loss(y_batch, y_pred)
            epoch_losses.append(loss)

            # Compute accuracy for classification
            if self.task_type == 'classification':
                y_pred_labels = np.argmax(y_pred, axis=1)
                accuracy = accuracy_score(y_batch, y_pred_labels)
                epoch_accuracies.append(accuracy)

            # Compute gradients and update weights
            gradients = self._compute_gradients(X_batch, y_batch, self.weights)
            self._update_weights(gradients)

        # Record epoch statistics
        epoch_loss = np.mean(epoch_losses)
        self.loss_history.append(epoch_loss)

        if self.task_type == 'classification' and epoch_accuracies:
            epoch_accuracy = np.mean(epoch_accuracies)
            self.accuracy_history.append(epoch_accuracy)

            if epoch % 10 == 0:
                logger.info(f"Epoch {epoch}: Loss = {epoch_loss:.4f}, Accuracy = {epoch_accuracy:.4f}")
        else:
            if epoch % 10 == 0:
                logger.info(f"Epoch {epoch}: Loss = {epoch_loss:.4f}")

        # Early stopping check
        if len(self.loss_history) > 10 and self._check_early_stopping():
            logger.info(f"Early stopping at epoch {epoch}")
            break

    self.is_fitted = True

    # Final training statistics
    final_loss = self.loss_history[-1]
    logger.info(f"Training completed. Final loss: {final_loss:.4f}")

    return self

def fit(self, X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, **kwargs) -> 'HybridClassifier':
    """Train the hybrid classifier.

    Args:
        X: Training data features
        y: Training data labels
        **kwargs: Additional training parameters

    Returns:
        Self for method chaining

    """
    logger.info(f"Training HybridClassifier on {X.shape[0]} samples with {X.shape[1]} features")

    # Validate and preprocess data
    super().fit(X, y, **kwargs)

    # Normalize features
    if self.normalize_data:
        X = self.scaler.fit_transform(X)

    # Encode labels
    y_encoded = self.label_encoder.fit_transform(y)

    # Apply feature selection
    X_selected = self._apply_feature_selection(X, y_encoded)

    # Train quantum models
    self.quantum_scores = self._train_quantum_models(X_selected, y_encoded)

    # Train classical models
    self.classical_scores = self._train_classical_models(X_selected, y_encoded)

    # Train meta-learner for stacking mode
    if self.hybrid_mode == 'stacking' and self.meta_learner is not None:
        logger.info("Training meta-learner for stacking")

        # Get base model predictions for meta-training
        quantum_preds, classical_preds = self._get_base_predictions(X_selected)

        meta_features = []
        if len(quantum_preds) > 0:
            for pred_proba in quantum_preds:
                meta_features.append(pred_proba)
        if len(classical_preds) > 0:
            for pred_proba in classical_preds:
                meta_features.append(pred_proba)

        if meta_features:
            meta_X = np.concatenate(meta_features, axis=1)
            self.meta_learner.fit(meta_X, y_encoded)

    # Train sequential model if needed
    if self.hybrid_mode == 'sequential':
        # Retrain classical models with quantum features
        quantum_features = []

        for name, model in self.quantum_models.items():
            try:
                if hasattr(model, 'transform'):
                    features = model.transform(X_selected)
                elif hasattr(model, 'decision_function'):
                    features = model.decision_function(X_selected)
                    if len(features.shape) == 1:
                        features = features.reshape(-1, 1)
                else:
                    features = model.predict_proba(X_selected)

                quantum_features.append(features)

            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Failed to extract features from {name}: {e}")

        if quantum_features:
            quantum_feature_matrix = np.concatenate(quantum_features, axis=1)

            # Retrain classical models with quantum features
            for name, model in self.classical_models.items():
                try:
                    model.fit(quantum_feature_matrix, y_encoded)
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.error(f"Failed to retrain {name} with quantum features: {e}")

    self.is_fitted = True

    # Compute hybrid performance
    predictions = self.predict(X)
    self.hybrid_score = accuracy_score(y, predictions)

    logger.info(f"Hybrid classifier training completed. Accuracy: {self.hybrid_score:.4f}")

    return self

def predict_proba(self, X: np.ndarray, **kwargs) -> np.ndarray:
    """Predict class probabilities.

    Args:
        X: Input data for prediction
        **kwargs: Additional parameters

    Returns:
        Predicted class probabilities

    """
    if not self.is_fitted:
        raise ValueError("Model must be fitted before making predictions")

    # Normalize features
    if self.normalize_data:
        X = self.scaler.transform(X)

    # Apply feature selection
    X_selected = self._apply_feature_selection(X)

    # Get base predictions
    quantum_preds, classical_preds = self._get_base_predictions(X_selected)

    if self.hybrid_mode == 'ensemble':
        # Weighted average of probabilities
        combined_pred = np.zeros((X.shape[0], self.n_classes_))

        if len(quantum_preds) > 0:
            quantum_avg = np.mean(quantum_preds, axis=0)
            combined_pred += self.quantum_weight * quantum_avg

        if len(classical_preds) > 0:
            classical_avg = np.mean(classical_preds, axis=0)
            combined_pred += (1 - self.quantum_weight) * classical_avg

        return combined_pred

    elif self.hybrid_mode == 'stacking' and self.meta_learner is not None:
        # Use meta-learner probabilities
        meta_features = []

        if len(quantum_preds) > 0:
            for pred_proba in quantum_preds:
                meta_features.append(pred_proba)
        if len(classical_preds) > 0:
            for pred_proba in classical_preds:
                meta_features.append(pred_proba)

        if meta_features:
            meta_X = np.concatenate(meta_features, axis=1)
            if hasattr(self.meta_learner, 'predict_proba'):
                return self.meta_learner.predict_proba(meta_X)

    # Fallback: convert predictions to probabilities
    predictions = self.predict(X)
    pred_encoded = self.label_encoder.transform(predictions)
    prob_matrix = np.zeros((len(predictions), self.n_classes_))
    prob_matrix[np.arange(len(predictions)), pred_encoded] = 1.0

    return prob_matrix

            'hybrid_vs_best_quantum': self.hybrid_score - best_quantum if self.hybrid_score else 0,

    return performance

def fit(self, X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray | None = None, **kwargs) -> 'QuantumPCA':
    """Fit quantum PCA to the data.

    Args:
        X: Training data
        y: Ignored (unsupervised learning)
        **kwargs: Additional fitting parameters

    Returns:
        Self for method chaining

    """
    logger.info(f"Fitting QuantumPCA to data of shape {X.shape}")

    # Validate and preprocess data
    super().fit(X, y, **kwargs)

    # Prepare data
    X_processed = self._prepare_data_matrix(X)

    # Determine quantum circuit size
    self.n_qubits = self._determine_qubits(X.shape[1])

    # Choose quantum method
    if self.method == 'vqe':
        density_matrix = self._create_density_matrix(X_processed)
        eigenvalues, eigenvectors = self._quantum_eigensolver_vqe(density_matrix)
    elif self.method == 'phase_estimation':
        density_matrix = self._create_density_matrix(X_processed)
        eigenvalues, eigenvectors = self._quantum_phase_estimation(density_matrix)
    elif self.method == 'matrix_inversion':
        density_matrix = self._create_density_matrix(X_processed)
        eigenvalues, eigenvectors = self._quantum_matrix_inversion(density_matrix)
    elif self.method == 'qsvd':
        eigenvalues, eigenvectors = self._quantum_svd(X_processed)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown quantum PCA method: {self.method}")

    # Store results
    self.eigenvalues_ = eigenvalues
    self.components_ = eigenvectors.T  # Store as rows
    self.explained_variance_ = eigenvalues

    # Calculate explained variance ratio
    total_variance = np.sum(eigenvalues) if np.sum(eigenvalues) > 0 else 1.0
    self.explained_variance_ratio_ = eigenvalues / total_variance

    # Fit classical PCA for comparison/fallback
    if self.classical_fallback:
        try:
            self.classical_pca.fit(X_processed)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Classical PCA fitting failed: {e}")

    self.is_fitted = True

    logger.info(f"Quantum PCA completed. Explained variance ratio: {self.explained_variance_ratio_}")

    return self

def transform(self, X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Transform data to lower dimensional space.

    Args:
        X: Data to transform

    Returns:
        Transformed data

    """
    if not self.is_fitted:
        raise ValueError("QuantumPCA must be fitted before transform")

    # Preprocess data
    if self.normalize_data:
        X = self.scaler.transform(X)

    # Center data
    X_centered = X - self.mean_

    # Project onto principal components
    X_transformed = X_centered @ self.components_.T

    return X_transformed

def inverse_transform(self, X_transformed: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Reconstruct data from lower dimensional representation.

    Args:
        X_transformed: Transformed data

    Returns:
        Reconstructed data

    """
    if not self.is_fitted:
        raise ValueError("QuantumPCA must be fitted before inverse_transform")

    # Reconstruct in original space
    X_reconstructed = X_transformed @ self.components_

    # Add back the mean
    X_reconstructed += self.mean_

    # Inverse scaling if applied
    if self.normalize_data:
        X_reconstructed = self.scaler.inverse_transform(X_reconstructed)

    return X_reconstructed

def get_quantum_advantage_metrics(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Analyze potential quantum advantage."""
    if not self.is_fitted:
        raise ValueError("Must fit model first")

    n_features = self.components_.shape[1]

    metrics = {
        'data_dimension': n_features,
        'reduced_dimension': self.n_components,
        'compression_ratio': n_features / self.n_components,
        'quantum_circuit_qubits': self.n_qubits,
        'quantum_vs_classical_qubits': self.n_qubits / int(np.ceil(np.log2(n_features))),
    }

    # Potential speedup estimates (theoretical)
    classical_complexity = n_features ** 3  # O(d^3) for eigendecomposition
    quantum_complexity = self.n_qubits ** 2 * np.log(n_features)  # Estimated quantum complexity

    metrics.update({
        'classical_complexity_estimate': classical_complexity,
        'quantum_complexity_estimate': quantum_complexity,
        'theoretical_speedup': classical_complexity / quantum_complexity if quantum_complexity > 0 else 1,
    })

    return metrics

def compare_with_classical(self, X: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compare quantum PCA results with classical PCA."""
    if not self.is_fitted or not hasattr(self.classical_pca, 'components_'):
        raise ValueError("Both quantum and classical PCA must be fitted")

    # Transform data with both methods
    X_quantum = self.transform(X)
    X_classical = self.classical_pca.transform(X - self.mean_)

    # Compute reconstruction errors
    X_quantum_reconstructed = self.inverse_transform(X_quantum)
    X_classical_reconstructed = self.classical_pca.inverse_transform(X_classical) + self.mean_

    quantum_error = np.mean((X - X_quantum_reconstructed) ** 2)
    classical_error = np.mean((X - X_classical_reconstructed) ** 2)

    # Compare explained variance
    quantum_var_ratio = np.sum(self.explained_variance_ratio_)
    classical_var_ratio = np.sum(self.classical_pca.explained_variance_ratio_)

    # Component similarity (using absolute cosine similarity)
    component_similarities = []
    min_components = min(self.n_components, len(self.classical_pca.components_))

    for i in range(min_components):
        # Cosine similarity between components
        cos_sim = np.abs(np.dot(self.components_[i], self.classical_pca.components_[i]))
        cos_sim /= (np.linalg.norm(self.components_[i]) * np.linalg.norm(self.classical_pca.components_[i]))
        component_similarities.append(cos_sim)

    return {
        'quantum_reconstruction_error': quantum_error,
        'classical_reconstruction_error': classical_error,
        'error_ratio': quantum_error / classical_error if classical_error > 0 else float('inf'),
        'quantum_variance_explained': quantum_var_ratio,
        'classical_variance_explained': classical_var_ratio,
        'variance_explained_ratio': quantum_var_ratio / classical_var_ratio if classical_var_ratio > 0 else float('inf'),
        'component_similarities': component_similarities,
        'mean_component_similarity': np.mean(component_similarities) if component_similarities else 0,
    }

def analyze_convergence(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Analyze convergence properties of the quantum algorithm."""
    if not self.convergence_history:
        return {'message': 'No convergence history available'}

    convergence_data = np.array(self.convergence_history)

    return {
        'total_iterations': len(convergence_data),
        'final_cost': convergence_data[-1],
        'initial_cost': convergence_data[0],
        'cost_reduction': convergence_data[0] - convergence_data[-1],
        'converged': abs(convergence_data[-1] - convergence_data[-2]) < self.tolerance if len(convergence_data) > 1 else False,
        'convergence_rate': np.mean(np.diff(convergence_data)) if len(convergence_data) > 1 else 0,
    }

def fit(self, X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray | None = None, **kwargs) -> 'QuantumKMeans':
    """Fit quantum K-means to the data.

    Args:
        X: Training data
        y: Ignored (unsupervised learning)
        **kwargs: Additional fitting parameters

    Returns:
        Self for method chaining

    """
    logger.info(f"Fitting QuantumKMeans to data of shape {X.shape}")

    # Validate and preprocess data
    super().fit(X, y, **kwargs)

    # Normalize data if specified
    if self.normalize_data:
        X = self.scaler.fit_transform(X)

    # Determine quantum circuit requirements
    self.n_qubits = self._determine_qubits(X.shape[1])

    # Initialize centroids
    centroids = self._initialize_centroids(X)

    # Reset convergence history
    self.convergence_history = []

    # Main K-means iteration loop
    for iteration in range(self.max_iterations):
        # Store old centroids for convergence check
        old_centroids = centroids.copy()

        # Compute distances and assign clusters
        distances = self._compute_distances_batch(X, centroids)
        labels = self._assign_clusters(distances)

        # Update centroids
        centroids = self._update_centroids(X, labels)

        # Compute inertia
        inertia = self._compute_inertia(X, labels, centroids)
        self.convergence_history.append(inertia)

        # Check convergence
        if self._check_convergence(old_centroids, centroids):
            logger.info(f"Converged after {iteration + 1} iterations")
            break

        if iteration % 10 == 0:
            logger.info(f"Iteration {iteration}: Inertia = {inertia:.6f}")

    # Store final results
    self.cluster_centers_ = centroids
    self.labels_ = labels
    self.inertia_ = inertia
    self.n_iter_ = iteration + 1

    # Fit classical K-means for comparison
    if self.classical_fallback:
        try:
            self.classical_kmeans.fit(X)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Classical K-means fitting failed: {e}")

    self.is_fitted = True

    logger.info(f"Quantum K-means completed. Final inertia: {self.inertia_:.6f}")

    return self

def get_quantum_advantage_metrics(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Analyze potential quantum advantage."""
    if not self.is_fitted:
        raise ValueError("Must fit model first")

    n_features = self.cluster_centers_.shape[1]
    n_samples = self.n_samples_

    metrics = {
        'data_dimension': n_features,
        'n_samples': n_samples,
        'n_clusters': self.n_clusters,
        'quantum_circuit_qubits': self.n_qubits,
        'encoding_efficiency': n_features / self.n_qubits if self.n_qubits > 0 else 1,
    }

    # Complexity estimates
    classical_complexity = n_samples * self.n_clusters * n_features * self.n_iter_
    quantum_complexity = n_samples * self.n_clusters * self.n_qubits * self.shots * self.n_iter_

    metrics.update({
        'classical_complexity_estimate': classical_complexity,
        'quantum_complexity_estimate': quantum_complexity,
        'theoretical_speedup': classical_complexity / quantum_complexity if quantum_complexity > 0 else 1,
    })

    return metrics

def compare_with_classical(self, X: np.ndarray, y_true: np.ndarray | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compare quantum K-means results with classical K-means."""
    if not self.is_fitted or not hasattr(self.classical_kmeans, 'cluster_centers_'):
        raise ValueError("Both quantum and classical K-means must be fitted")

    # Get predictions from both methods
    quantum_labels = self.predict(X)
    classical_labels = self.classical_kmeans.predict(X if not self.normalize_data
                                                    else self.scaler.transform(X))

    comparison = {
        'quantum_inertia': self.inertia_,
        'classical_inertia': self.classical_kmeans.inertia_,
        'inertia_ratio': self.inertia_ / self.classical_kmeans.inertia_ if self.classical_kmeans.inertia_ > 0 else float('inf'),
        'quantum_iterations': self.n_iter_,
        'classical_iterations': self.classical_kmeans.n_iter_,
    }

    # Compute silhouette scores
    try:
        if len(np.unique(quantum_labels)) > 1:
            quantum_silhouette = silhouette_score(X, quantum_labels)
            comparison['quantum_silhouette'] = quantum_silhouette

        if len(np.unique(classical_labels)) > 1:
            classical_silhouette = silhouette_score(X, classical_labels)
            comparison['classical_silhouette'] = classical_silhouette

        if 'quantum_silhouette' in comparison and 'classical_silhouette' in comparison:
            comparison['silhouette_ratio'] = quantum_silhouette / classical_silhouette

    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"Silhouette score computation failed: {e}")

    # Compare with ground truth if available
    if y_true is not None:
        try:
            quantum_ari = adjusted_rand_score(y_true, quantum_labels)
            classical_ari = adjusted_rand_score(y_true, classical_labels)

            comparison.update({
                'quantum_adjusted_rand_score': quantum_ari,
                'classical_adjusted_rand_score': classical_ari,
                'ari_ratio': quantum_ari / classical_ari if classical_ari != 0 else float('inf'),
            })

        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Adjusted rand score computation failed: {e}")

    # Compare centroid similarities
    centroid_distances = []
    for i in range(min(len(self.cluster_centers_), len(self.classical_kmeans.cluster_centers_))):
        dist = np.linalg.norm(self.cluster_centers_[i] - self.classical_kmeans.cluster_centers_[i])
        centroid_distances.append(dist)

    if centroid_distances:
        comparison.update({
            'centroid_distances': centroid_distances,
            'mean_centroid_distance': np.mean(centroid_distances),
            'max_centroid_distance': np.max(centroid_distances),
        })

    return comparison

Bases: OptimizationQuantumAlgorithm

Variational Quantum Eigensolver for finding ground states.

VQE is a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm that uses a parameterized quantum circuit (ansatz) to find the ground state energy of a given Hamiltonian by minimizing the expectation value.

The algorithm works by: 1. Preparing a parameterized quantum state |ψ(θ)⟩ 2. Measuring the expectation value ⟨ψ(θ)|H|ψ(θ)⟩ 3. Classically optimizing parameters θ to minimize energy 4. Iterating until convergence

def get_energy_landscape(self, param_indices: list[int], param_ranges: list[tuple[float, float]],
                       resolution: int = 20) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compute energy landscape for visualization.

    Args:
        param_indices: Indices of parameters to vary
        param_ranges: Ranges for each parameter
        resolution: Number of points per dimension

    Returns:
        Dictionary with landscape data

    """
    if len(param_indices) != 2:
        raise ValueError("Energy landscape visualization supports only 2 parameters")

    if self.optimal_params_ is None:
        raise ValueError("VQE must be optimized to compute landscape")

    param1_range = np.linspace(*param_ranges[0], resolution)
    param2_range = np.linspace(*param_ranges[1], resolution)

    landscape = np.zeros((resolution, resolution))
    base_params = self.optimal_params_.copy()

    for i, p1 in enumerate(param1_range):
        for j, p2 in enumerate(param2_range):
            params = base_params.copy()
            params[param_indices[0]] = p1
            params[param_indices[1]] = p2
            landscape[i, j] = self._compute_expectation_value(params)

    return {
        'param1_range': param1_range,
        'param2_range': param2_range,
        'landscape': landscape,
        'optimal_params': self.optimal_params_[param_indices],
        'param_indices': param_indices
    }

def analyze_convergence(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Analyze VQE convergence properties.

    Returns:
        Convergence analysis results

    """
    if not self.energy_history:
        raise ValueError("No optimization history available")

    energies = np.array(self.energy_history)
    gradients = np.array(self.gradient_history) if self.gradient_history else None

    # Basic convergence metrics
    analysis = {
        'final_energy': energies[-1],
        'energy_variance': np.var(energies[-10:]) if len(energies) >= 10 else np.var(energies),
        'total_iterations': len(energies),
        'energy_change': abs(energies[-1] - energies[0]) if len(energies) > 1 else 0,
    }

    # Convergence detection
    if len(energies) >= 10:
        recent_change = abs(energies[-1] - energies[-10])
        analysis['converged'] = recent_change < self.convergence_threshold
    else:
        analysis['converged'] = False

    # Gradient analysis
    if gradients is not None and len(gradients) > 0:
        analysis.update({
            'final_gradient_norm': gradients[-1],
            'gradient_trend': 'decreasing' if gradients[-1] < gradients[0] else 'increasing',
            'min_gradient_norm': np.min(gradients),
        })

    # Identify plateaus and oscillations
    if len(energies) >= 20:
        # Check for plateaus (little change over many iterations)
        plateau_threshold = self.convergence_threshold * 10
        recent_energies = energies[-20:]
        energy_std = np.std(recent_energies)
        analysis['plateau_detected'] = energy_std < plateau_threshold

        # Check for oscillations
        energy_diff = np.diff(energies[-20:])
        sign_changes = np.sum(np.diff(np.sign(energy_diff)) != 0)
        analysis['oscillation_detected'] = sign_changes > len(energy_diff) * 0.7

    return analysis

def compare_with_exact(self, exact_ground_energy: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compare VQE result with exact ground state energy.

    Args:
        exact_ground_energy: Known exact ground state energy

    Returns:
        Comparison analysis

    """
    if self.optimal_value_ is None:
        raise ValueError("VQE must be optimized for comparison")

    error = abs(self.optimal_value_ - exact_ground_energy)
    relative_error = error / abs(exact_ground_energy) if exact_ground_energy != 0 else float('inf')

    return {
        'vqe_energy': self.optimal_value_,
        'exact_energy': exact_ground_energy,
        'absolute_error': error,
        'relative_error': relative_error,
        'chemical_accuracy': error < 1.6e-3,  # 1 kcal/mol in Hartree
        'energy_above_ground': max(0, self.optimal_value_ - exact_ground_energy)
    }

def find_ground_state(self) -> float:
    """Find the ground state energy of the Hamiltonian.

    This is a convenience method that combines fit() and _run_optimization()
    to find the ground state energy in a single call.

    Returns:
        Ground state energy

    Example:
        >>> vqe = VQE(backend='simulator', hamiltonian=hamiltonian)

def create_vqe_for_molecule(
    molecule_name: str,
    bond_distance: float | None = None,
    backend: str = 'simulator',
    ansatz: str = 'RealAmplitudes',
    optimizer: str = 'COBYLA',
    client = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> VQE:
    """Create a VQE instance for a small molecule.

    Only H2 in STO-3G at its equilibrium bond length (0.735 Angstrom) ships
    with the library. Other molecules or bond lengths need a Hamiltonian from
    a chemistry package (e.g. PySCF + OpenFermion or Qiskit Nature) passed to
    :class:`VQE` directly.
    """
    if molecule_name.upper() != 'H2':
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"No built-in Hamiltonian for {molecule_name}. Build one with a chemistry "
            "package and pass it to VQE(hamiltonian=...)."
        )
    if bond_distance is not None and abs(bond_distance - 0.735) > 0.02:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "Only the H2 equilibrium geometry (0.735 Angstrom) is built in."
        )
    return VQE(
        hamiltonian=dict(H2_STO3G_0735),
        ansatz=ansatz,
        backend=backend,
        optimizer=optimizer,
        client=client,
        **kwargs,
    )

QAOA(backend: str | Any, p: int = 1, problem_hamiltonian: Callable | None = None, mixer_hamiltonian: Callable | None = None, initial_state: str = 'uniform_superposition', optimizer: str = 'COBYLA', shots: int = 1024, maxiter: int = 1000, n_restarts: int = 3, **kwargs)

Bases: OptimizationQuantumAlgorithm

Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for combinatorial optimization.

QAOA is a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm that alternates between quantum evolution and classical parameter optimization to find approximate solutions to combinatorial optimization problems.

The algorithm works by: 1. Preparing an initial superposition state 2. Applying alternating problem and mixer Hamiltonians 3. Measuring the quantum state 4. Classically optimizing the parameters

def __init__(
    self,
    backend: str | Any,
    p: int = 1,
    problem_hamiltonian: Callable | None = None,
    mixer_hamiltonian: Callable | None = None,
    initial_state: str = 'uniform_superposition',
    optimizer: str = 'COBYLA',
    shots: int = 1024,
    maxiter: int = 1000,
    n_restarts: int = 3,
    **kwargs
) -> None:
    super().__init__(backend=backend, shots=shots, **kwargs)

    self.p = p
    self.n_restarts = n_restarts
    self.problem_hamiltonian = problem_hamiltonian
    self.mixer_hamiltonian = mixer_hamiltonian or self._default_mixer
    self.initial_state = initial_state
    self.optimizer = optimizer
    self.maxiter = maxiter

    # QAOA-specific parameters
    self.n_qubits = None
    self.problem_instance = None
    self.circuit = None

    # Parameter bounds
    self.gamma_bounds = (0, 2*np.pi)
    self.beta_bounds = (0, np.pi)

    logger.info(f"Initialized QAOA with p={p}, optimizer={optimizer}")

def fit(self, X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray | None = None, **kwargs) -> 'QAOA':
    """Fit QAOA to problem instance.

    Args:
        X: Problem instance data (e.g., adjacency matrix for Max-Cut)
        y: Not used in QAOA
        **kwargs: Additional parameters

    Returns:
        Self for method chaining

    """
    logger.info(f"Fitting QAOA to problem instance of shape {X.shape}")

    self.problem_instance = X
    self.n_qubits = self._infer_qubits(X)

    # Reset optimization history
    self.optimization_history_ = []

    self.is_fitted = True
    return self

def predict(self, X: np.ndarray | None = None, **kwargs) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sample the optimised circuit and return the best sampled partition.

    Entry i of the returned 0/1 array is the side of node i.
    """
    if not self.is_fitted or self.optimal_params_ is None:
        raise ValueError("QAOA must be fitted and optimized before prediction")
    circuit = self._create_qaoa_circuit(self.optimal_params_)
    samples = self.backend.sample_circuit(circuit, shots=self.shots)
    unique = np.unique(samples, axis=0)
    values = [cut_value(self.problem_instance, row) for row in unique]
    return unique[int(np.argmax(values))]

def solve(self, adjacency: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Fit, optimise and sample in one call, with an exact classical check.

    Returns the QAOA partition and cut, the brute-force optimum, and the
    approximation ratio of the expected QAOA cut.
    """
    self.fit(np.asarray(adjacency, dtype=float))
    result = self._run_optimization(None)
    bits = self.predict()
    best_bits, best_cut = brute_force_maxcut(self.problem_instance)
    return {
        'bitstring': ''.join(str(int(b)) for b in bits),
        'cut_value': cut_value(self.problem_instance, bits),
        'expected_cut': self.optimal_value_,
        'classical_bitstring': ''.join(str(int(b)) for b in best_bits),
        'classical_optimum': best_cut,
        'approximation_ratio': self.optimal_value_ / best_cut if best_cut else float('nan'),
        'optimal_params': self.optimal_params_,
        'n_evaluations': result['n_iterations'],
    }

def get_optimization_landscape(self, param_range: tuple[float, float], resolution: int = 50) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Compute optimization landscape for visualization.

    Args:
        param_range: Range of parameters to explore
        resolution: Number of points per dimension

    Returns:
        Dictionary with landscape data

    """
    if self.p != 1:
        logger.warning("Landscape visualization only supported for p=1")
        return {}

    gamma_range = np.linspace(*param_range, resolution)
    beta_range = np.linspace(*param_range, resolution)

    landscape = np.zeros((resolution, resolution))

    for i, gamma in enumerate(gamma_range):
        for j, beta in enumerate(beta_range):
            params = np.array([gamma, beta])
            landscape[i, j] = -self._objective_function(params)

    return {
        'gamma_range': gamma_range,
        'beta_range': beta_range,
        'landscape': landscape,
        'optimal_params': self.optimal_params_ if hasattr(self, 'optimal_params_') else None
    }

def analyze_solution_quality(self, true_optimum: float | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Analyze quality of QAOA solution.

    Args:
        true_optimum: Known optimal value for comparison

    Returns:
        Analysis results

    """
    if self.optimal_value_ is None:
        raise ValueError("No optimal solution available")

    analysis = {
        'qaoa_value': self.optimal_value_,
        'n_layers': self.p,
        'n_parameters': 2 * self.p,
        'optimization_iterations': len(self.optimization_history_),
    }

    if true_optimum is not None:
        approximation_ratio = self.optimal_value_ / true_optimum
        analysis.update({
            'true_optimum': true_optimum,
            'approximation_ratio': approximation_ratio,
            'relative_error': abs(1 - approximation_ratio),
        })

    # Analyze convergence
    if len(self.optimization_history_) > 1:
        costs = [-entry['cost'] for entry in self.optimization_history_]
        analysis.update({
            'convergence_achieved': costs[-1] == max(costs),
            'improvement_over_random': self.optimal_value_ - np.mean(costs[:5]) if len(costs) >= 5 else 0,
            'final_cost_variance': np.var(costs[-10:]) if len(costs) >= 10 else 0,
        })

    return analysis

QuantumPortfolioAgent(backend: str | Any, n_select: int | None = None, risk_aversion: float = 1.0, reps: int = 2, alpha: float = 0.25, n_restarts: int = 5, maxiter: int = 300, **kwargs)

Bases: QuantumAgent

Pick k of n assets with CVaR-VQE, checked against exact classical answers.

The selection problem is encoded as a diagonal Ising Hamiltonian whose ground state is the best equal-weight k-asset portfolio. A RealAmplitudes circuit is trained on the chosen backend to minimise the CVaR of the energy (the mean of the best alpha fraction of outcomes, Barkoutsos et al., Quantum 4, 256 (2020)), which works much better than the plain expectation for combinatorial problems. shots samples are drawn from the final state and the best sampled selection is returned. Two classical references are always computed in the same call: the brute-force optimum of the same QUBO and a long-only Markowitz solution with continuous weights. Practical up to about 10 assets (2^n statevector).

def fit(self, X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray | None = None, **kwargs) -> QuantumPortfolioAgent:
    """Estimate mean returns and covariance from a (periods x assets) matrix."""
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)

def solve(self, problem_instance: np.ndarray | None = None, **kwargs) -> QuantumResult:
    """Select assets with VQE and report the classical checks.

    Args:
        problem_instance: Optional returns matrix; refits the agent if given.

    Returns:
        QuantumResult whose ``result`` has the quantum selection and weights,
        its objective, the brute-force optimum, whether they match, the
        probability VQE puts on the optimal selection, and a classical
        Markowitz reference.

    """
    start = time.time()
    if problem_instance is not None:
        self.fit(problem_instance)
    if not self.is_fitted:
        raise ValueError("Call fit(returns) or pass returns to solve()")

    n = len(self.expected_returns)
    k = self.n_select or max(1, n // 2)
    values = portfolio_qubo_values(self.expected_returns, self.covariance_matrix, k,
                                   self.risk_aversion)
    # Rescale so feasible selections span [0, 1]: same ground state, but the
    # optimizer sees the differences that matter instead of the penalty wall.
    feasible = np.array([bin(i).count('1') == k for i in range(2 ** n)])
    spread = max(values[feasible].max() - values[feasible].min(), 1e-12)
    H = np.diag((values - values.min()) / spread)

    order = np.argsort(H.diagonal())
    h_sorted = H.diagonal()[order]
    n_params = self.backend.ansatz_param_count('RealAmplitudes', n, reps=self.reps)

    def probabilities(params):
        circuit = self.backend.create_ansatz('RealAmplitudes', n, params, reps=self.reps)
        return np.abs(self.backend.statevector_big_endian(circuit)) ** 2

    def cvar(params):
        # Mean energy of the best alpha fraction of the distribution (exact, from probabilities).
        p_sorted = probabilities(params)[order]
        cum = np.cumsum(p_sorted)
        take = np.clip(self.alpha - (cum - p_sorted), 0.0, p_sorted)
        return float(np.sum(take * h_sorted) / self.alpha)

    base_seed = 0 if self.seed is None else self.seed
    best = None
    for r in range(max(1, self.n_restarts)):
        x0 = np.random.default_rng(base_seed + r).uniform(-np.pi, np.pi, n_params)
        res = minimize(cvar, x0, method='COBYLA', options={'maxiter': self.maxiter})
        if best is None or res.fun < best.fun:
            best = res
    probs = probabilities(best.x)
    probs = probs / probs.sum()
    samples = np.random.default_rng(base_seed).choice(len(probs), size=self.shots, p=probs)
    q_index = int(samples[np.argmin(values[samples])])
    c_index = int(np.argmin(values))
    self.optimal_params_ = best.x

    def bits(i):
        return np.array([(i >> (n - 1 - j)) & 1 for j in range(n)])

    q_bits, c_bits = bits(q_index), bits(c_index)
    weights = q_bits / max(1, q_bits.sum())
    self.optimal_weights = weights

    result = {
        'selected_assets': [int(i) for i in np.flatnonzero(q_bits)],
        'weights': weights,
        'objective': float(values[q_index]),
        'cvar_rescaled': float(best.fun),
        'shots': self.shots,
        'feasible': bool(q_bits.sum() == k),
        'classical_selected_assets': [int(i) for i in np.flatnonzero(c_bits)],
        'classical_objective': float(values[c_index]),
        'matches_classical_optimum': bool(q_index == c_index),
        'objective_gap': float(values[q_index] - values[c_index]),
        'probability_of_optimum': float(probs[c_index]),
        'optimum_sampled': bool(np.any(samples == c_index)),
        'markowitz_reference': self._markowitz(),
        **self._metrics(weights),
    }
    self.performance_metrics = {k_: result[k_] for k_ in
                                ('matches_classical_optimum', 'probability_of_optimum')}
    return self._result(result, start, n_assets=n, n_select=k,
                        method='CVaR-VQE on a mean-variance QUBO; brute force check',
                        n_evaluations=int(best.nfev))

def solve(self, problem_instance: Any = None, **kwargs) -> QuantumResult:
    """Solve and return the quantum answer with its exact classical check."""
    start = time.time()
    if problem_instance is not None:
        self.fit(problem_instance)
    if self.problem_instance is None:
        raise ValueError("Pass an adjacency matrix (combinatorial) or Hamiltonian (continuous)")

    if self.problem_type == 'combinatorial':
        out = self.algorithms['qaoa'].solve(np.asarray(self.problem_instance, dtype=float))
        out['matches_classical_optimum'] = bool(
            np.isclose(out['cut_value'], out['classical_optimum']))
        return self._result(out, start, problem_type='maxcut', algorithm_used='QAOA',
                            classical_check='brute force')

    vqe = self.algorithms['vqe']
    vqe.fit(self.problem_instance)
    opt = vqe._run_optimization()
    out = {
        'ground_energy': opt['ground_energy'],
        'exact_energy': opt['exact_energy'],
        'error': abs(opt['ground_energy'] - opt['exact_energy']),
        'optimal_params': opt['optimal_params'],
        'n_evaluations': opt['n_iterations'],
    }
    return self._result(out, start, problem_type='ground_state', algorithm_used='VQE',
                        classical_check='exact diagonalisation')

        'algorithms': self.available_algorithms, 'ensemble_method': ensemble_method,

docs.text:
fit(X: ndarray, y: ndarray, **kwargs) -> QuantumClassificationAgent

Fit every algorithm. Errors propagate; nothing is silently scored as 0.

Source code in src/superquantx/algorithms/quantum_agents.py 
def fit(self, X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, **kwargs) -> QuantumClassificationAgent:
    """Fit every algorithm. Errors propagate; nothing is silently scored as 0."""
    for name, algorithm in self.algorithms.items():
        algorithm.fit(X, y)
        self.performance_metrics[name] = {
            'train_accuracy': float(accuracy_score(y, algorithm.predict(X)))
        }
    self.is_fitted = True
    return self

docs.title: predict
docs.text:
predict(X: ndarray, **kwargs) -> np.ndarray

Predict with one algorithm, or combine several.

Source code in src/superquantx/algorithms/quantum_agents.py 
def predict(self, X: np.ndarray, **kwargs) -> np.ndarray:
    """Predict with one algorithm, or combine several."""
    if not self.is_fitted:
        raise ValueError("Agent must be fitted before prediction")
    preds = {name: np.asarray(a.predict(X)) for name, a in self.algorithms.items()}
    if len(preds) == 1:
        return next(iter(preds.values()))
    if self.ensemble_method == 'best':
        best = max(self.performance_metrics,
                   key=lambda n: self.performance_metrics[n]['train_accuracy'])
        return preds[best]
    weights = {n: (self.performance_metrics[n]['train_accuracy']
                   if self.ensemble_method == 'weighted' else 1.0) for n in preds}
    out = []
    for i in range(len(X)):
        votes: dict[Any, float] = {}
        for n, p in preds.items():
            votes[p[i]] = votes.get(p[i], 0.0) + weights[n]
        out.append(max(votes.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])[0])
    return np.array(out)

docs.title: solve
docs.text:
solve(problem_instance: tuple[ndarray, ndarray], **kwargs) -> QuantumResult

Benchmark against classical baselines with CV, then fit on all data.

Keyword arguments are passed to compare_to_classical.

Source code in src/superquantx/algorithms/quantum_agents.py 
def solve(self, problem_instance: tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray], **kwargs) -> QuantumResult:
    """Benchmark against classical baselines with CV, then fit on all data.

    Keyword arguments are passed to ``compare_to_classical``.
    """
    from ..benchmarks import compare_to_classical

    start = time.time()
    X, y = problem_instance
    name, algorithm = next(iter(self.algorithms.items()))
    kwargs.setdefault('cv', self.cv)
    kwargs.setdefault('seed', 0 if self.seed is None else self.seed)
    benchmark = compare_to_classical(X, y, algorithm, **kwargs)
    self.fit(X, y)
    result = {
        'algorithm': name,
        'cv_accuracy': benchmark.quantum.accuracy_mean,
        'cv_accuracy_std': benchmark.quantum.accuracy_std,
        'best_classical': benchmark.best_classical.name,
        'best_classical_cv_accuracy': benchmark.best_classical.accuracy_mean,
        'delta_vs_best_classical': benchmark.delta_vs_best_classical,
        'p_value': benchmark.p_value_vs_best_classical,
        'verdict': benchmark.verdict,
        'benchmark': benchmark,
        'train_accuracy': self.performance_metrics[name]['train_accuracy'],
    }
    return self._result(result, start, n_samples=len(X), n_features=X.shape[1],
                        n_classes=len(np.unique(y)), algorithms_used=list(self.algorithms))

docs.title: Comparing Algorithms
docs.text:
import time
import numpy as np
from sklearn.datasets import make_classification
import superquantx as sqx

X, y = make_classification(
    n_samples=40, n_features=2, n_informative=2, n_redundant=0, random_state=0
)

def time_fit(ctor, **kwargs):
    model = ctor(**kwargs)
    t0 = time.time()
    model.fit(X, y)
    return time.time() - t0, float(np.mean(model.predict(X) == y))

for name, ctor, kwargs in [
    ("QuantumSVM", sqx.QuantumSVM, {"backend": "simulator", "feature_map": "ZFeatureMap"}),
    ("QuantumNN", sqx.QuantumNN, {"backend": "simulator", "n_layers": 1, "max_epochs": 8, "seed": 0}),
]:
    secs, acc = time_fit(ctor, **kwargs)
    print(f"{name}: acc={acc:.3f} in {secs:.2f}s")

docs.title: Circuits API Reference
docs.text:
This page covers circuit construction, gate matrices, Pauli strings and Hamiltonians, measurement results and noise channels. The usage examples at the end run on SuperQuantX 0.3.0.

Two kinds of circuit

  • Backend circuits come from backend.create_circuit(n) and are built with backend.add_gate(...) or, on the simulator, with methods such as circuit.h(0). These are what backend.execute_circuit runs.
  • superquantx.QuantumCircuit is a backend-independent circuit description that can be drawn, composed, inverted and serialised to JSON. In 0.3.0 no backend executes it directly.

QuantumCircuit(num_qubits: int, num_classical_bits: int | None = None, name: str | None = None)

Quantum circuit representation with gate operations and measurements

This class provides a high-level interface for building and manipulating quantum circuits compatible with multiple quantum computing frameworks.

Initialize a quantum circuit

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default num_qubits int

Number of qubits in the circuit

required num_classical_bits int | None

def __init__(
    self,
    num_qubits: int,
    num_classical_bits: int | None = None,
    name: str | None = None
):
    """Initialize a quantum circuit

    Args:
        num_qubits: Number of qubits in the circuit
        num_classical_bits: Number of classical bits (defaults to num_qubits)
        name: Optional circuit name

    """
    self.num_qubits = num_qubits
    self.num_classical_bits = num_classical_bits or num_qubits
    self.name = name or f"circuit_{id(self)}"

    self.quantum_registers: list[QuantumRegister] = [
        QuantumRegister(name="q", size=num_qubits)
    ]
    self.classical_registers: list[ClassicalRegister] = [
        ClassicalRegister(name="c", size=self.num_classical_bits)
    ]

    self.gates: list[QuantumGate] = []
    self.measurements: list[tuple[int, int]] = []  # (qubit_index, classical_bit_index)
    self.barriers: list[list[int]] = []  # Barrier positions

def add_register(self, register: QuantumRegister | ClassicalRegister) -> None:
    """Add a quantum or classical register to the circuit"""
    if isinstance(register, QuantumRegister):
        self.quantum_registers.append(register)
        self.num_qubits += register.size
    elif isinstance(register, ClassicalRegister):
        self.classical_registers.append(register)
        self.num_classical_bits += register.size

def compose(self, other: "QuantumCircuit", qubits: list[int] | None = None) -> "QuantumCircuit":
    """Compose this circuit with another circuit

    Args:
        other: Circuit to compose with
        qubits: Qubit mapping for the other circuit

    Returns:
        New composed circuit

    """
    if qubits is None:
        qubits = list(range(other.num_qubits))

    if len(qubits) != other.num_qubits:
        raise ValueError("Qubit mapping must match other circuit size")

    new_circuit = self.copy()

    # Map gates from other circuit
    for gate in other.gates:
        mapped_qubits = [qubits[q] for q in gate.qubits]
        new_gate = QuantumGate(
            name=gate.name,
            qubits=mapped_qubits,
            parameters=gate.parameters,
            classical_condition=gate.classical_condition
        )
        new_circuit.gates.append(new_gate)

    # Map measurements
    for qubit, cbit in other.measurements:
        new_circuit.measurements.append((qubits[qubit], cbit))

    return new_circuit

def inverse(self) -> "QuantumCircuit":
    """Return the inverse (adjoint) of the circuit"""
    inv_circuit = QuantumCircuit(self.num_qubits, self.num_classical_bits)

        inv_circuit.gates.append(inv_gate)
